license_notes: Annotations: urinieto/harmonixset (MIT, annotations only — Harmonix Music Systems / ISMIR 2019). Audio: YouTube-sourced per the upstream youtube_urls.csv, fetched locally with yt-dlp, never redistributed. Mel spectrograms of the ORIGINAL audio distributed by the authors via Dropbox (the alignment-gate reference).

sources.name: annotations
sources.notes: dataset/beats_and_downbeats/<id>.txt = 'time<TAB>beat_in_bar<TAB>bar' (beat_in_bar 1 = downbeat); dataset/segments/<id>.txt = 'start label' rows (last row is the end marker); metadata.csv carries Duration/BPM/Genre; youtube_urls.csv + youtube_alignment_scores.csv drive the fetch and the gate prior; jams/ carries librosa onsets of the first 30 s of the ORIGINAL audio (the offset-estimation reference). The pinned clone IS the track list — coverage is computed from its CSVs, not duplicated here.

sources.name: audio
sources.notes: yt-dlp (Python API, bestaudio) per youtube_urls.csv into raw/yt/, then ffmpeg -> FLAC 44.1 kHz in audio/. Re-fetched YouTube audio is not byte-reproducible and may be a different master/edit — that is exactly what the alignment gate exists for; per-track hashes are status.json observations. Unavailable/region-locked/removed videos are normal per-track failures.

sources.name: melspecs
sources.notes: ~1.2 GB, mel spectrograms of the original (annotation-matching) audio + info.json with parameters — the whole-track DTW reference for the alignment gate. sha256 pinned after first verified fetch.

gate.notes: Pilot findings (2026-08-07, first 40 tracks): (1) fetched videos are typically LONGER than annotated — official music videos embed the song behind intros/skits — so subsequence mel-DTW against the authors' distributed melspecs is BOTH the offset estimator (path median) and the whole-span verifier (on-line fraction + median residual), and prep cuts the FLAC to the aligned span (annotation times stay on the original clock); (2) the JAMS-onset xcorr cannot be a wide-window gate (true matches peak at r~0.4-0.55, indistinct from noise) — it is the sub-frame REFINEMENT of the DTW offset in a narrow window, gated only on agreement; (3) the shorter-duration check compares against the last annotation time, not metadata Duration (which counts trailing silence).

notes: gate.calibrated flips to true after the C12 threshold calibration on ~20 hand-checked tracks; prep refuses to emit bundles for tracks without a pass* verdict.

Drop ground truth: the segment vocabulary has NO drop/build labels (verified from the paper + files) — tier 1 = /(^|_)drop/ label matches (expected ~zero, reported), tier 2 = non-chorus->chorus* transitions on Genre in {Dance/Electronic, Dubstep} as kind proxy_chorus_onset. Tiers never merge in reporting.
